title: Crown and Garden
premise: Theo Amberdale, a bone-carver who hears the voices of the dead, has survived five years in Vellamarch by hiding his gift after magic was outlawed. When he discovers tonight's date inscribed in a century-old book of prophecies — with his own name beside it — he is hunted by the Crown's Inquisitors and sheltered by the Gardeners, an underground network of outlaws who dispense justice the law abandoned. Guided by the ghost of the last dragon and a prophecy that names him as 'the door,' Theo must find the threshold out of Vellamarch, a country that officially no longer exists on any map, before the dragon-fire sustaining its hidden borders gutters out forever. In the end, Theo learns the door is not a place but a choice: he must burn his own bones' memory to relight the fire, erasing his gift and his past, and choose to stay in a reborn Vellamarch rather than escape it.
about_author: Jonah Thornbury is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about quiet people caught in loud histories, and live somewhere with too many doors.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't Tomorrow
chapters.summary: Theo carves a mourning charm for a widow while the dead murmur their usual grievances, then finds today's date inked in a forbidden prophecy book sold to him by mistake. His name sits beneath it. POV: Theo. Beat: dread disguised as ordinary life shattering.

chapters.title: Knock at the Bone-Shop
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Hale arrives asking polite questions about unlicensed charms; Theo lies badly and burns the prophecy page, but the ash spells his name again. POV: Theo. Beat: fear tightening into certainty that he is already caught.

chapters.title: The Gardener's Mark
chapters.summary: A stranger named Wren Sallow spirits Theo through the tenements using chalk sigils, revealing the Gardeners — healers, forgers, and thieves who answer crimes the law ignores. POV: Theo. Beat: reluctant wonder at a world of belonging he never had.

chapters.title: What the Dead Remember of Dragons
chapters.summary: In the Gardeners' root-cellar sanctuary, a ghost attached to an old dragon-bone speaks: it is Ember-of-Ashes, last dragon, and it knows the prophecy. POV: Theo. Beat: grief meeting kinship across death.

chapters.title: Hale's Ledger
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Hale, POV chapter: she suspects the bone-carver but her real quarry is the Gardeners, whose vigilante justice humiliated her family years ago. Beat: antagonist made sympathetic; duty versus doubt.

chapters.title: The Country Off the Map
chapters.summary: Ember explains Vellamarch was erased from treaties a century ago; its true borders persist only where dragon-fire still burns, invisible and dying. The prophecy's 'door' leads out of it. POV: Theo. Beat: vertigo — his whole life has been inside a lie.

chapters.title: Charms for the Drowned Quarter
chapters.summary: To earn his keep, Theo works a Gardeners' case: finding a drowned child's killer the courts refused to prosecute. The dead boy tells him where. POV: Theo. Beat: justice outside the law feels right and terrifying.

chapters.title: Wren's Price
chapters.summary: Wren reveals she joined the Gardeners after the Crown executed her brother on false testimony; she needs Theo's gift to clear other names. POV: Wren. Beat: loyalty forged from shared wounds, with an edge of using him.

chapters.title: The First Guttering
chapters.summary: Dragon-fire flickers citywide; wards fail for one terrible minute and Inquisitor patrols pour into old streets that shouldn't exist. POV: Theo. Beat: countdown begins — the country is literally going out.

chapters.title: Ashes That Spell Names
chapters.summary: Theo experiments with burning prophecy pages; each ash reveals a fragment: a door, a crown, a garden, and a figure holding his own carved bones. POV: Theo. Beat: fascination curdling into foreboding.

chapters.title: The Widow's Testimony
chapters.summary: The widow from chapter one is arrested for possessing Theo's charm; the Gardeners debate rescuing her, risking exposure. Theo insists. POV: Theo. Beat: his first choice to act rather than hide.

chapters.title: Raid on the Root-Cellar
chapters.summary: Hale's raid nearly succeeds; Wren's quick thinking saves the sanctuary but a young Gardener is taken. POV: Wren. Beat: victory tasting like loss; the network's first crack.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Hale questions the captured Gardener, who says nothing — but Hale finds a carved bone charm and recognizes Theo's handiwork. POV: Hale. Beat: the net closing; her admiration for the prisoner complicates her zeal.

chapters.title: The Ghost Market
chapters.summary: Theo and Wren seek a smuggler who trades in dead men's memories, hoping to learn what 'the door' means. The market's dead recognize Ember's voice in Theo. POV: Theo. Beat: awe and violation — even the dead have black markets.

chapters.title: Ember's Confession
chapters.summary: The dragon admits it let the borders die slowly, weary of guarding a country that betrayed it; the prophecy was its own dying wish, not fate. POV: Theo. Beat: anger at being conscripted by a ghost's despair.

chapters.title: Prison Break at Low Tide
chapters.summary: The Gardeners spring the captured youth through the flooded cisterns; Theo hears the dead prisoners guiding them out. POV: Wren. Beat: triumph, and Theo realizing his curse is a compass.

chapters.title: Hale Follows the Chalk
chapters.summary: Hale decodes the Gardener sigils and maps the sanctuary district, but hesitates to report it — a superior's cruelty makes her question whose justice she serves. POV: Hale. Beat: antagonist's loyalty fracturing.

chapters.title: The Prophecy Read Backward
chapters.summary: An exiled scholar reveals the prophecy reads differently in reverse: the door doesn't lead out of Vellamarch — it leads the country back into existence. POV: Theo. Beat: revelation reframing everything; hope with a cost.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Bone Orchard
chapters.summary: Theo visits his mother's grave; her ghost confesses she bound his hearing-gift deliberately to protect him from a previous purge. POV: Theo. Beat: betrayal and forgiveness tangled; belonging redefined.

chapters.title: The Crown's Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Court intrigue: the Regent plans to let Vellamarch's wards fail entirely, annexing the land legally once it 'doesn't exist.' POV: Hale, summoned to court. Beat: scale widens; personal stakes become national.

chapters.title: Betrayal in Green Chalk
chapters.summary: A Gardener informant sells the sanctuary's location to buy his daughter's pardon; Wren discovers it and must choose mercy or exile for him. POV: Wren. Beat: loyalty versus truth tearing the found-family.

chapters.title: Evacuation of the Garden
chapters.summary: The Gardeners scatter to safehouses; Theo refuses to leave without Ember's bone, which is hidden beneath the root-cellar. POV: Theo. Beat: stubborn love for a place about to be lost.

chapters.title: What Hale Found in the Cellar
chapters.summary: Hale reaches the cellar first, holds Ember's bone, and hears the dragon herself — the dead speak to her too, faintly. POV: Hale. Beat: the antagonist's worldview cracks open.

chapters.title: Truce in the Cistern Dark
chapters.summary: Cornered together during a ward-collapse, Theo and Hale strike an uneasy truce: she wants the truth about the purge her superiors buried; he wants the bone back. POV: alternating. Beat: enemies recognizing shared purpose.

chapters.title: The Purge Papers
chapters.summary: Hale delivers sealed records: the outlawing of magic was staged to erase Vellamarch's sovereignty, and her own family signed it. POV: Hale. Beat: devastating truth; loyalty to the Crown becomes impossible.

chapters.title: Regent's Hunt
chapters.summary: The Regent declares martial law over the invisible districts; Wren's network becomes open rebellion whether they chose it or not. POV: Wren. Beat: reluctant warriors; no more shadows to hide in.

chapters.title: Ember's Last Bright Hour
chapters.summary: The dragon-fire gutters to embers; streets flicker between existing and not, and citizens wake remembering a country they were made to forget. POV: Theo. Beat: mass awakening; grief and fury in the streets.

chapters.title: The Door Is a Person
chapters.summary: The backward prophecy completes: the door is 'a maker who carries the dead' — Theo himself, his bones the key, his gift the hinge. POV: Theo. Beat: destiny accepted at last, though the price is unnamed.

chapters.title: Sacrifice Named Aloud
chapters.summary: Ember tells the price: relighting the fire requires burning the bone-memory of a living maker — Theo will lose his gift, his ghosts, every voice he's ever loved. POV: Theo. Beat: the cost made flesh; despair before resolve.

chapters.title: Wren's Argument
chapters.summary: Wren begs Theo to flee through the failing border instead — she can't lose another person she loves to a cause. POV: Wren. Beat: love weaponized against duty; the theme's sharpest edge.

chapters.title: March of the Remembering
chapters.summary: Thousands of awakened citizens march on the Regent's hall carrying candles and carved bones; Hale publicly defects, reading the purge papers aloud. POV: Hale. Beat: catharsis; justice erupting outside every law.

chapters.title: The Regent's Fire
chapters.summary: The Regent orders the last wards burned to force annexation; the palace quarter blinks out of existence with people inside. POV: Theo, feeling their deaths. Beat: horror at the stakes made mortal and immediate.

chapters.title: Into the Hearth of the Country
chapters.summary: Theo, Wren, and Hale fight through collapsing streets to the First Hearth where Vellamarch's fire was lit a century ago. POV: Theo. Beat: relentless momentum; the country literally dissolving around them.

chapters.title: Ember's Choice
chapters.summary: At the Hearth, Ember offers to take Theo's place — but a ghost's memory cannot light a living flame. The dragon asks forgiveness instead of sacrifice. POV: Theo. Beat: heartbreak; even dragons cannot save him from choosing.

chapters.title: The Burning of Theo Amberdale
chapters.summary: Climax: Theo lays his carved bones and his gift upon the Hearth and lets the fire take them, screaming farewell to every dead voice, including his mother's. POV: Theo. Beat: climax — total loss embraced willingly.

chapters.title: A Country Relit
chapters.summary: Dragon-fire roars back through the borders; Vellamarch blazes back onto maps and memory; the Regent's claim collapses mid-signature. POV: Wren watching from the crowd. Beat: exultation shadowed by Theo's silence.

chapters.title: Silence Where the Voices Were
chapters.summary: Theo wakes deaf to the dead, hollowed, unable to feel the belonging he bought for everyone else. Wren refuses to let him vanish into that hollowness. POV: Theo. Beat: the dark night after victory.

chapters.title: Trials in the Open Square
chapters.summary: Vellamarch rebuilds its courts; Hale testifies against her former order, and the Gardeners must answer for their extralegal justice too. POV: Hale. Beat: justice institutionalized imperfectly; no clean hands.

chapters.title: New Bones, Old Hands
chapters.summary: Theo carves again — plain charms with no magic — and finds the work itself, not the voices, was always his calling. A child's ghost lingers near him, unheard but felt. POV: Theo. Beat: quiet healing; identity rebuilt.

chapters.title: The Door Left Open
chapters.summary: One year later: Vellamarch stands, the Gardeners are its sworn magistrates, and Theo plants a garden over the old root-cellar with Wren. He keeps the door unlocked — for anyone, living or dead, seeking belonging. POV: Theo. Beat: resolution — home chosen, not escaped to.
